name: NUCLEO-F446ZE (STM32F446ZE)
description: ST's NUCLEO-F446ZE (MB1137): an STM32F446ZET6 clocked from the ST-LINK's 8 MHz MCO, with a 32.768 kHz crystal, the user LEDs LD1 (green, PB0), LD2 (blue, PB7) and LD3 (red, PB14), the blue USER button B1 on PC13 (active high), the black RESET button B2, the power LED LD6, JP3 choosing the 5 V source (U5V, VIN, E5V or CHGR), JP5 (IDD) to measure the MCU's current, the ST Zio connectors CN7 to CN10 (Arduino Uno V3 and more), the two ST morpho headers CN11 and CN12 reaching every I/O, and the USB OTG FS connector CN13. The ST-LINK/V2-1's virtual COM port is the session's serial console on USART3 (PD8/PD9), and a serial port on the host (embsim serve --serial).

components.doc: LD1117S50TR: 5 V from VIN (7 to 12 V) for JP3's VIN position
U5V's power switch: joins the ST-LINK's USB 5 V to JP3's U5V position once the ST-LINK pulls PWR_ENn low
The switch's gate pull-up to U5V: off until the ST-LINK enables it
The ST-LINK's PWR_ENn output driving low (it has enumerated and the host granted 300 mA)
JP3 (PWR) on U5V: the board runs from the ST-LINK's USB (the factory position)
JP3 (PWR) on VIN: the board runs from VIN through U3
JP3 (PWR) on E5V: the board runs from an external 5 V on CN11 pin 6
JP3 (PWR) on CHGR: the ST-LINK's USB 5 V straight to +5V, without the power switch (a USB charger that does not enumerate)
LD39050PU33R: +3.3V from +5V (500 mA)
JP5 (IDD): +3.3V to the STM32's VDD; remove it and put an ammeter across IDD_3V3 and IDD_VDD
LD6 (PWR): +5V is present
LD1 (USER, green): PB0 high lights it (SB120 on, SB119 off)
LD2 (USER, blue): PB7 high lights it
LD3 (USER, red): PB14 high lights it
B1 USER (blue): pulls PC13 up to VDD while pressed (active high, as ST's BSP reads it)
B1's series resistor to PC13 (with C_B1, a 10 us filter)
B1's pull-down on PC13: low while B1 is released
B1's filter capacitor on PC13
B2 RESET (black): pulls NRST low
NRST's capacitor: with the STM32's internal pull-up, it holds the part in reset for about 1.5 ms at power-on
VCAP_1: one of the two low-ESR ceramics the core regulator needs on a part with VCAP_1 and VCAP_2
VCAP_2
BOOT0 pull-down: the part boots its flash
X2: the 32.768 kHz crystal on PC14/PC15 (6 pF load, 50 kOhm ESR maximum), the same equivalent circuit as the NUCLEO-F446RE's
The solder bridge (on) joining VDDA and VREF+ to VDD
ST Zio, right top (2 x 10): D8..D25 with D14/D15 (I2C), AREF, GND
ST Zio, left top (2 x 8): the Arduino power pins and D43..D50 (SDMMC)
ST Zio, left bottom (2 x 15): A0..A5 and D51..D72
ST Zio, right bottom (2 x 17): D0..D7, A6..A8, D26..D42
ST morpho, left (2 x 35)
ST morpho, right (2 x 35)
USB OTG FS, micro-AB: VBUS, D-, D+, ID, GND

5V.doc: +5V: an output from USB, VIN or E5V through JP3

VIN.doc: 7 to 12 V into U3 (LD1117S50); JP3 must be on VIN

A4.doc: PF5 by default; PB9 (I2C1_SDA) with the solder bridges moved

A5.doc: PF10 by default; PB8 (I2C1_SCL) with the solder bridges moved

D56.doc: PE2, also D31 on CN10 pin 25

D31.doc: PE2, also D56 on CN9 pin 14

D33.doc: PB0, also the green LED LD1

CN11_6.doc: E5V: an external 5 V supply in (JP3 on E5V)

CN11_29.doc: PH0 (OSC_IN) carries the ST-LINK's 8 MHz MCO; the morpho pin is not joined to it in the factory state

CN11_31.doc: PH1 (OSC_OUT): not joined to the morpho pin in the factory state

CN11_69.doc: PD9, USART3_RX: the ST-LINK VCP's TX drives it

CN12_10.doc: PD8, USART3_TX: the ST-LINK VCP's RX listens to it

USB_VBUS.doc: VBUS of the USB OTG connector, sensed on PA9 (OTG_FS_VBUS)

U5V.doc: The ST-LINK's USB 5 V (CN1, micro-B) from the host; also CN12 pin 8

IDD_3V3.doc: JP5 pin 1, the regulator's side: an ammeter's + lead

IDD_VDD.doc: JP5 pin 2, the STM32's side: an ammeter's - lead

functional.claims: Nets, ports, LD1, LD2, LD3, LD6, B1, B2 and the jumpers as parts; the STM32F446ZE runs its firmware (see its description), its HSE an 8 MHz clock on PH0 (HSEBYP needed, as on the real board) and its LSE the X2 crystal. The ST Zio connectors CN7 to CN10 carry UM1974's pin assignment for the NUCLEO-F446ZE (the Arduino Uno V3 subset D0 to D15 and A0 to A5, and D16 to D72, A6 to A8) and the morpho headers CN11 and CN12 every one of the part's 114 I/Os; CN13 joins PA9 (VBUS), PA11 (D-), PA12 (D+) and PA10 (ID). The ST-LINK/V2-1's virtual COM port is the session's console on USART3 (PD8/PD9) and a serial port on the host.
omissions: the ST-LINK/V2-1 itself: its USB enumeration, the mass-storage drag-and-drop programming, SWD and its NRST drive (the session programs and debugs the board, ADR-031)
the VCP's bytes reach USART3 directly, not as frames on PD9

the USB OTG FS controller (no model yet: CN13's lines are the pins alone), the USB power switch U12 (STMPS2151STR: PG6 its enable, PG7 its over-current flag) and its LEDs LD7 (VBUS) and LD8 (over-current)
the solder bridges are fixed in their factory state (LD1 on PB0, A4 on PF5 and A5 on PF10, CN11 pins 29 and 31 not joined to PH0/PH1, PD8/PD9 to the ST-LINK)
one JP3 shunt sits on one position only; the four switches here can all be closed
the ST-LINK's own over-current LED and limit on U5V
CN4 (SWD to an external target) and the ST-LINK's CN1 beyond its 5 V

electrical.claims: The power paths of UM1974's power supply section: the ST-LINK's USB 5 V (U5V) through its power switch (enabled by PWR_ENn low) to JP3's U5V position, or straight to its CHGR position; VIN (7 to 12 V) through U3 (LD1117S50) to its VIN position; E5V to its E5V position; U4 (LD39050PU33R) makes +3.3V from +5V and JP5 (IDD) carries it to VDD, VBAT, VDDUSB, PDR_ON and (through a solder bridge) VDDA and VREF+. LD6 shows +5V; LD1, LD2 and LD3 are lit by PB0, PB7 and PB14 high through 510 ohm; B1 pulls PC13 up to VDD through 100 ohm against a 4.7 kOhm pull-down, a 100 nF capacitor filtering it; a 100 nF capacitor holds NRST low for about 1.5 ms at power-on against the STM32's pull-up; VCAP_1 and VCAP_2 have 2.2 uF each; a 10 kOhm resistor holds BOOT0 low; X2 is the NUCLEO-F446RE's crystal's equivalent circuit.
omissions: MB1137's schematic was not at hand: the user LEDs' and the power LED's resistors, B1's resistors and capacitor and the NRST and VCAP capacitors take the NUCLEO-F446RE's (MB1136's) values or the datasheet's recommendation, and the U5V power switch is the MB1136's P-MOSFET; reference designators beyond those UM1974 names (LDx, Bx, JPx, CNx) are EmbSIM's
the ST-LINK's current negotiation: PWR_ENn is low as after a host has granted 300 mA
the ST-LINK's own supply and current
the STM32's supply current: VDD carries only what the pins drive, so with JP5 removed and no ammeter VDD floats instead of falling to 0 V, and the STM32 keeps running whatever VDD is

provenance.notes: Artwork is an original SVG drawn for EmbSIM to the board's 70 x 133.34 mm outline; no ST artwork or logo is used. The morpho pin assignment (CN11, CN12) places each of the 114 I/Os once. The morpho assignment matches, pin for pin, CN11 and CN12 of ST's MB1364 C-01 schematic (the Nucleo-144 board of the NUCLEO-H743ZI, sheet 5), whose morpho headers carry the same LQFP144 pins; MB1364's board-specific parts (its transistor-driven LEDs, LD2 on PE1, its USB switch enabled from PD10, the ST-LINK-V3E) are not MB1137's and none of its values is used here.
